cards.title: Uranus is the coldest planet in the solar system, beating even Neptune
cards.body: Although Neptune is much farther from the Sun, Uranus holds the solar system's record for the lowest planetary atmosphere temperature ever measured. Deep in its cloud decks, temperatures plunge to minus 224 degrees Celsius. Unlike other giant planets, Uranus releases very little internal heat, leaving its upper atmosphere exceptionally frigid.

cards.title: Light takes up to 100,000 years to escape from inside the Sun
cards.body: Photons of light are generated by nuclear fusion deep in the Sun's core. Because solar plasma is so dense, a photon repeatedly collides with electrons and protons in a random path. It takes between 10,000 and 100,000 years for light to scatter to the surface, though once free, it reaches Earth in eight minutes.

cards.title: Humanity's most distant robotic landing occurred on Saturn's moon Titan
cards.body: In January 2005, the European Space Agency's Huygens probe descended through the dense methane haze of Titan, Saturn's largest moon. Touching down nearly 1.4 billion kilometers from Earth, it became the most distant landing ever accomplished. The probe survived on the frozen surface for over two hours, transmitting images of icy river pebbles.

cards.title: The first discovered pulsar was initially named after alien life
cards.body: When astronomer Jocelyn Bell Burnell detected a remarkably steady radio pulse every 1.33 seconds in 1967, scientists were baffled by its unnatural regularity. Unsure of its origin, the research team jokingly cataloged the signal as LGM-1, short for 'Little Green Men 1.' They soon realized it was actually a rapidly spinning neutron star.

cards.title: Astronauts on the Space Station watch 16 sunrises and sunsets every day
cards.body: Orbiting Earth at roughly 28,000 kilometers per hour, the International Space Station completes a full trip around the planet every 90 minutes. Because of this extreme speed, crew members experience a sunrise or sunset every 45 minutes, totaling 16 of each every 24 hours. Astronauts use set lighting schedules to maintain normal sleep rhythms.

cards.title: A magnetar's magnetic field is strong enough to destroy data thousands of miles away
cards.body: Magnetars are an extreme type of neutron star boasting magnetic fields a quadrillion times stronger than Earth's. If a magnetar were situated halfway to the Moon, its magnetic pull would easily wipe the magnetic strips on every credit card across Earth. At closer distances, its field would tear apart electron clouds, dismantling molecular chemistry.

cards.title: A single gamma-ray burst produces more energy than the Sun will in its entire lifetime
cards.body: Gamma-ray bursts are the most violent electromagnetic explosions in the universe, triggered by massive collapsing stars or merging neutron stars. In just a few seconds, a powerful gamma-ray burst can release more energy than our Sun will generate over its entire 10-billion-year existence. If one occurred nearby, it could strip Earth's protective ozone layer.

cards.title: The Moon isn't round—it's shaped like a slightly lopsided egg
cards.body: Viewed from Earth, the Moon appears as a neat circle, but gravitational interactions shaped it differently. Over billions of years, tidal forces exerted by Earth pulled the Moon's crust into an elongated, egg-like shape. Its smaller, pointier end points toward Earth, and its center of mass sits roughly 2 kilometers off-center.

cards.title: Without gravity to walk on, astronauts shed the skin on the bottoms of their feet
cards.body: Because astronauts do not walk on surfaces in microgravity, calluses on the soles of their feet gradually soften and peel off during long missions. Crew members frequently report shedding thick layers of dead skin when taking off their socks, forcing them to carefully strip foot calluses near airflow filtration vents to avoid floating debris.

cards.title: Earth shares its orbit with companion asteroids trapped at gravitational sweet spots
cards.body: Earth isn't traveling alone in its path around the Sun. Gravitational balances between the Sun and Earth create stable regions known as Lagrange points. In 2020, astronomers confirmed 2020 XL5, a kilometer-wide Trojan asteroid locked into Earth's L4 point. It leads Earth along its orbital trail and will remain trapped in this orbit for millennia.

quizzes.question: Which planet in our solar system holds the record for the lowest recorded atmosphere temperature?
quizzes.explanation: Although Neptune is farther from the Sun, Uranus reaches lower atmospheric temperatures (-224°C) due to low internal heat release.

quizzes.question: How long can light take to travel from the Sun's core to its surface?
quizzes.explanation: Dense plasma causes light particles to constantly scatter, taking tens of thousands of years to bounce out to the surface.

quizzes.question: Where did humanity's most distant spacecraft landing take place?
quizzes.explanation: The Huygens probe landed on Titan in 2005, making it the most distant landing from Earth in history.

quizzes.question: Why was the first discovered pulsar radio signal designated 'LGM-1'?
options: It was named after astronomer Louis G. Miller
Scientists jokingly referred to it as 'Little Green Men 1'
It was recorded at the Lunar Gravitational Observatory
quizzes.explanation: Because of its startlingly precise pulses, researchers playfully designated the signal 'Little Green Men 1'.

quizzes.question: How many sunrises and sunsets do astronauts on the International Space Station see every 24 hours?
quizzes.explanation: Orbiting Earth every 90 minutes, ISS astronauts experience 16 sunrises and 16 sunsets each day.

quizzes.question: What extreme physical body possesses magnetic fields strong enough to wipe credit cards from hundreds of thousands of kilometers away?
quizzes.explanation: Magnetars are ultra-dense neutron stars with magnetic fields powerful enough to erase magnetic media from lunar distances.

quizzes.question: How much energy can a single gamma-ray burst emit in just a few seconds?
options: As much energy as Earth uses in one year
More energy than the Sun releases in its entire 10-billion-year lifespan
Roughly equal to a large solar flare
As much energy as an atomic explosion
quizzes.explanation: Gamma-ray bursts are cosmic explosions capable of releasing more energy in seconds than our Sun will generate across its full life.

quizzes.question: What shape is the Moon brought into by gravitational interactions with Earth?
quizzes.explanation: Tidal forces stretched the Moon into a slightly elongated egg shape pointing towards Earth.

quizzes.question: Why do astronauts experience skin peeling off the bottoms of their feet during space missions?
options: Loss of calluses due to not walking in weightlessness
Radiation exposure in low Earth orbit
quizzes.explanation: Without gravity forcing feet against ground, old foot calluses soften and slough off in microgravity.

quizzes.question: What is 2020 XL5, which shares Earth's orbit around the Sun?
quizzes.explanation: 2020 XL5 is a Trojan asteroid trapped at the L4 Lagrange point ahead of Earth in its orbital path.

guesses.prompt: How many years can light take to bounce from the Sun's core to its outer surface?
guesses.explanation: Due to dense solar interior scattering, photons spend between 10,000 and 100,000 years traveling to the Sun's surface.

guesses.prompt: How many sunrises do astronauts on the International Space Station witness in a single 24-hour day?
guesses.explanation: Because the ISS orbits Earth every 90 minutes, crew members see 16 sunrises and 16 sunsets every day.

guesses.prompt: What is the expected lifespan of our Sun in billions of years?
guesses.explanation: The Sun will generate energy for approximately 10 billion years—an amount rivaled in seconds by a single gamma-ray burst.

misconceptions.claim: Neptune is the coldest planet in the solar system because it is farthest from the Sun.
misconceptions.explanation: Uranus holds the record for the coldest recorded planetary temperature (-224°C) because it emits very little internal heat compared to Neptune.

misconceptions.claim: The first discovered pulsar was playfully designated with an acronym referring to alien life.
misconceptions.explanation: Astronomers initially cataloged the mysterious, regular signals as LGM-1, short for 'Little Green Men 1'.

misconceptions.claim: The Earth's Moon is a symmetrical sphere.
misconceptions.explanation: Gravitational tidal tugs from Earth have stretched the Moon into an asymmetrical, slightly egg-like shape.
